identity.title: Kinematics of the ionized and molecular gas in nearby luminous infrared interacting galaxies
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: combined the observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) observations of these systems in CO emission to compare the physical properties of the star formation regions and the molecular gas clouds

question.value: How do the star formation rate and molecular gas surface densities and internal kinematics of HII regions and molecular clouds in interacting LIRGs compare with those in normal galaxies and high-z extreme star-forming galaxies?

evidence.quote: we will explore the connection between the high SFR, and molecular gas surface densities in HII regions and molecular clouds in LIRGs, compared them with normal star forming regions, and extreme star forming regions at higher redshifts.

method.value: Dendrograms on Halpha and CO data cubes to extract flux, radius, velocity dispersion

evidence.quote: to extract the basic properties of the clouds (flux, radius, and velocity dispersion): the HII regions from the GH$\alpha$FaS data-cubes, and the molecular clouds from the ALMA data-cubes.
We followed the procedure (the bootstrapping method) explained in (cite: 2006PASP..118..590R) to derive the errors in the measured parameters.

method.value: SFR from Halpha luminosity (Kennicutt 1998), electron density, ionized mass, virial parameter

evidence.quote: $\rm{SFR}(\rm{M_{\odot}/yr})=7.9\cdot10^{-42}L_{\rm{H\alpha}}(\rm{erg/s})$

assumptions.value: E(B-V)=0.4 constant attenuation correction; spherical uniform-density HII regions

evidence.quote: we correct using the average value found for $E(B-V)=0.4$ in the HII regions identified in the Antennae galaxies

method.value: CO luminosity from Solomon et al. 1992, mass via alpha_CO, surface density and virial parameter

evidence.quote: $M_{\mathrm{H_2}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}\thinspace L_{\mathrm{CO}},$

key_parameters.value: alpha_CO = 4.8 Msun (K km/s pc2)^-1, multiplied by 1.8 for CO(3-2) in Arp 186 and 236; factor 1.36 for helium

evidence.quote: We adopt the value of $\alpha_{CO}=4.8\rm{M_{\odot}(K\thinspace km\thinspace s^{-1})^{-1}}$
the average ratio is $\frac{I_{CO}(1-0)}{I_{CO}(3-2)}\simeq1.8$

method.value: Radius-error-weighted linear fits of log relations, Pearson coefficient and reduced chi2; envelope regions chosen by minimum sigma per luminosity bin

evidence.quote: We fit separately radius error weighted linear fits to the $\log(\Sigma_{\rm{SFR}})=a\log\rm{SFR}+b$ relation

fitting.value: weighted linear least squares by radius error; 95% confidence bands

evidence.quote: We fit separately radius error weighted linear fits to the $\log(\Sigma_{\rm{SFR}})=a\log\rm{SFR}+b$ relation for the HII regions in the LIRGS, the Antennae, and for those in the non-interacting galaxy sample.
We estimate that the observed points are correlated using the Pearson Correlation Coefficient, and that the linear relation fits well enough through $\chi^2_{\rm{red}}$.
We made use of ASTRODENDRO, a Python package to compute dendrogramsof Astronomical data
This research made use of ASTROPY, a community-developed core Python package for Astronomy
APLPY, an open-source plotting package for Python
We identified and measured the properties of 23 HII regions in Arp 186, 46 in Arp 236, and 19 in Arp 298
and of 12 molecular clouds in Arp 186, 6 in Arp 236, and 9 in Arp 298
with an average value of $R_{\rm{eq}}=0.86\pm0.14$

findings_qualitative.value: Clouds with lower virial parameter have higher Sigma_SFR and Sigma_mol, i.e. are gravitationally dominated rather than pressure confined

evidence.quote: Since the virial parameter decreases with the surface densities of both the star formation rate and the molecular gas, we claim that the clouds presented here are gravitationally dominated

claims.hypothesis: Sigma_SFR-SFR relation is steeper for HII regions in LIRGs than in normal galaxies
claims.experiment: Weighted linear fits of log Sigma_SFR vs log SFR
claims.finding: SFR surface densities are enhanced in LIRGs, closer to high-z extreme systems

evidence.quote: We find that the $\Sigma_{\rm{SFR}}$-$\rm{SFR}$ relation is steeper for the HII regions in LIRGs compared to HII regions in normal star forming galaxies

claims.hypothesis: Sigma_mol-M_mol trend is steeper for GMCs in LIRGs
claims.finding: Trend seems steeper but needs better data

evidence.quote: due to the high dispersion of this relation, more quality data are needed to confirm the trend for GMCs.

claims.result: Trend of decreasing alpha_vir with increasing Sigma_SFR and Sigma_mol

evidence.quote: We present evidence here which supports the hypothesis that self-gravity is responsible for the enhancement of the molecular gas and SFR densities in the most massive clouds, notably in LIRGs.

why_this_data.value: LIRGs chosen because already observed with public ALMA data

evidence.quote: We selected these LIRGs because they have been already observed with ALMA, from which the data are publicly available.

limitations_admitted.value: alpha_CO uncertain; masses may be overestimated by factor up to 4 or underestimated by 3

evidence.quote: Thus, our estimates of the molecular gas masses could be overestimated by a factor up to 4, or underestimated by a factor of 3

referee_caveats_inferred: Resolution differences between samples may drive density trends
Ionized mass used for HII virial parameters
Uniform alpha_CO and constant dust attenuation assumed
